markdown: ## Watchlist - **HSBC:** It plans to merge its Singapore operations to simplify its regional structure, as it explores building up Singapore to balance its reliance on China [Reuters](https://news.google.?oc=5)[Bloomberg.com](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisAFBVV95cUxOV3FEcV8zUEdEWUJzVkZzeGVoNXJFOExfb3VXYlktY3B5TF9YMnh4SVV1ZURCdHNMWjVub0REWlNtQ0Zyc3ZwRzFjdndGcE5GQnMzTTVGUU5NWjFhMXZRa2lLNDM0MzdQc0xCSnV2WWthd3FpOVZha3c2d01CakRVUUVYUXk2WFFrOXl1clZ2WTYyRVYwQTlEUHBPNDlrTnQzc2owM1BTTlVlU0duWXVZQQ?oc=5). If you bank with HSBC in Asia, expect changes to legal entities and booking locations, so check what happens to account mandates, pooling structures and credit lines. - **HSBC:** It plans significant risk transfers on $7bn of US and Asian corporate loans [Bloomberg.com](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisgFBVV95cUxNY3lUSlZabmlJVHo4VlY0MHowNm5qYkxKN0NLa0pETHlpVlEwUDJVbTFZV092b2R6SFRGZFFrcmc3cWxhblNJZ1dURDVsakk4SWFNbmJxbFBlUjk4bW9DOXE1azNhNFZYOXl2Z1hXNGRib0ZTbU43dV9mMS14dlBkdHc5akFZYTY3VmY4Uno0ODdjckUzQnRWNU04Yzl2SGtoLTFOZUlzdHprOGlFS0w5X3V3?oc=5). This frees up capital to keep lending, which is supportive for corporate credit lines, but ask whether any of Carrier's facilities are in the pool. ## The brief - **Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned amid scandal, and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO** [CFO Dive](https://www.cfodive.com/news/nvidia-ceo-resigns-scandal-cfo-named-interim-ceo-ai/874479/). The shares fell as much as 14% before closing 5% down [Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/a93307a7-e2cd-4abd-bd89-c38832d8c40e?syn-25a6b1a6=1). Expect volatility in AI-linked credit and equity markets, which could spill over into broader risk appetite and funding spreads. - **A Reuters poll expects the ECB to make its last rate hike in December, with the door open to one more** [Reuters](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiswFBVV95cUxOc1hXaEpuRUhpTnBKTGNYQU9CNnJhRFBYNHdTb2VIOUVyU1VoNmNYcjhNRXdJVTZEQUR4Sm5neEFMOWhwRjF3UW9PLXJuRFNwNG5CSEF5d1hKUTNuQVM0ZXQ5cDBsR04tVDVaT2tGU0VVQWtsZmlNdjROS0ZNdXBUZWF1ZUFTbXZicUE4b0Z0RXo4M3Z6SzFsMXVfZV9QVGMxM1BuMFFZNXktTlloT2dvclB6MA?oc=5). Euro deposit and borrowing rates are likely to peak soon, so consider locking in longer euro deposits after the December move. - **There is a bipartisan push to curb presidential tariff powers**, with three bills in Congress that would significantly restrict them [Manufacturing Dive](https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/bipartisan-push-possible-to-curb-trump-tariffs/874502/). If any pass, tariff risk becomes more predictable, which would change sourcing and pricing scenarios in the 2027 plan. - **Oil prices rose after President Trump said no Iran deal was needed** [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/oil-prices-jump-after-trump-says-no-iran-deal-needed-weve-got-their-strait.html). The prospect of no end to the US-Iran war keeps energy, freight and input-cost risk alive. ## Rates & FX - **The US bond sell-off deepened.** The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.10% (+12bp on the day, +26bp on the week) and the 2-year is 4.86% (+40bp on the week). SOFR is still 3.89%. Term debt now costs over 5%, so revisit any refinancing plans and the fixed/floating mix. - **The dollar keeps climbing.** EUR/USD fell 0.41% to 1.1081 (-1.27% on the week) and GBP/USD fell to 1.3256 (-1.51% on the week). The dollar value of European earnings is being squeezed, so check hedge cover on Q4 conversions. - **Other currencies.** USD/JPY is 159.70 (+0.78% on the week) and USD/MXN is 18.691 (+0.54% on the week). USD/CNY is flat at 6.6683, and EUR/GBP is 0.8359. €STR is 2.439% and SONIA is 3.9837%. - **US PPI today at 13:30 Dublin**, forecast at +0.4% after +1.3%, with core at +0.3%. Another hot number could push the 10-year further above 5% and extend the dollar rally. ## Also worth knowing - **HSBC says the yuan's share of global payments could double as its use rises** [Bloomberg.com](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiswFBVV95cUxOSkx6bTMtVXhDcE04X0pfdEZXNXdLT1VuLWpiNE5PcXh6OFppYkdyNzFhUXgybW5Nck4xdUpqUi1mVmJJX09USWJ1NVo5TFF5d0ZLSzczYnRDMk11OXg5ZlhFSnUzSkVGUkpiVXozN3FqdXdiOFFFVWFYY3dYWXFJckt6ZDdpN0hvN1VDMXF3ekIzZHQzTl9KVjUyTzlzOV8td0twTGJTYjFZY3BoTElsWFhmNA?oc=5). That is worth factoring into CNY invoicing and settlement plans. - **AI spending ran 24% above expectations at organisations that overspent in the past year, according to Capgemini** [CFO Dive](https://www.cfodive.com/news/cfos-confront-cash-flow-risks-ai-costs-rise/874554/). CFOs are now confronting the cash-flow risks. - **From 2027 the Fed will hold seven voting meetings**, with the October meeting set aside for deliberation and no rate vote [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/in-policy-switch-fed-says-its-october-2027-meeting-will-not-see-a-vote-on-interest-rates.html). - **Hancock Whitney is buying Trustmark in a $3.2bn deal**, creating a lender with $58bn in assets [Banking Dive](https://www.bankingdive.com/news/hancock-whitney-buy-trustmark-3b-deal-bank-acquisition/874522/). ## Worth thinking about CNH is selling 70% of its construction equipment business to Kobelco for $700m, so it can focus only on agriculture [Manufacturing Dive](https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/cnh-sell-70-percent-stake-construction-equipment-business-kobelco/874497/). It is a clean example of narrowing a portfolio to a core franchise. With funding costs above 5%, a useful FP&A question is which parts of Carrier's own portfolio earn their cost of capital, and which would be worth more to another owner.
